skill.name: verification-before-completion
skill.description: Requires fresh verification evidence before reporting that work is complete, fixed, passing, or ready for delivery.
skill.summary: Verify work with current evidence before making completion claims.
skill.author: davila7

content.value_statement: Unverified completion claims create rework and reduce trust. This skill requires fresh command output and direct evidence before reporting success.
actual_capabilities: Requires fresh verification evidence before any completion claim.
Guides selection and execution of a command that proves the specific claim.
Requires review of full output, exit codes, and failure counts.
Distinguishes tests, linters, builds, bug checks, and requirement reviews.
Promotes independent verification of delegated work through diffs and checks.
limitations: Does not select project-specific verification commands automatically.
Does not execute tests, builds, linters, or version control operations itself.
Cannot ensure full coverage when the chosen verification command is incomplete.
Provides process guidance, not project-specific acceptance criteria.

use_cases.title: Validate a coding task
use_cases.description: Run targeted tests and inspect results before reporting that an implementation is complete.

use_cases.title: Review delegated changes
use_cases.description: Inspect version control changes and rerun checks before accepting an agent completion report.

use_cases.title: Confirm release readiness
use_cases.description: Verify builds, tests, and requirement checklists before approving a release candidate.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a completed task
prompt_templates.prompt: Verify this task before reporting completion. Identify the proving command, run it, inspect the full result, and report only evidence-supported status.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use after a small implementation or maintenance task.

prompt_templates.title: Confirm a bug fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Reproduce the original failure, run the targeted regression test, and report whether current evidence proves the bug is fixed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before closing a bug report.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a regression test
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a red-green verification: confirm passing behavior, remove the fix, confirm failure, restore the fix, and confirm passing behavior again.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when adding regression coverage for a defect.

prompt_templates.title: Audit release readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review every acceptance criterion, choose complete verification commands, run them, inspect all outputs and exit statuses, then report evidence and unresolved gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use before a pull request, release, or deployment decision.

output_examples.input: Claim that the full test suite passes.
output_examples.output: The suite completed with 34 tests passing, zero failures, and exit status 0. Current evidence supports the claim.

output_examples.input: Claim that the build is ready after running only the linter.
output_examples.output: The linter passed, but no build was run. Build readiness remains unverified.

output_examples.input: Claim that delegated changes satisfy every requirement.
output: The version control diff confirms the expected files changed.
Targeted tests pass with no failures.
One acceptance criterion lacks verification, so the task is not complete.

best_practices: Match each claim to a command or inspection that directly proves it.
Use fresh, complete output and check the exit status before reporting results.
Report failures and verification gaps with the same precision as successful checks.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on previous runs, partial checks, or expected outcomes.
Do not treat a passing linter as proof that tests or builds pass.
Do not accept an agent completion report without inspecting changes and rerunning relevant checks.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it before reporting success, committing changes, creating a pull request, closing a task, or moving to new work.

faq.question: Does the skill run verification commands?
faq.answer: It directs the active agent to run suitable commands. The skill contains no scripts or fixed commands.

faq.question: What counts as fresh evidence?
faq.answer: Fresh evidence is current output produced during the active task, including relevant results, failure counts, and exit status.

faq.question: Is a passing linter enough?
faq.answer: Only for a lint claim. It does not prove that compilation, tests, integration behavior, or requirements are correct.

faq.question: How should failed verification be reported?
faq.answer: State the actual result, cite the observed failure, and avoid completion language until the issue is resolved and rechecked.

faq.question: Can it verify delegated agent work?
faq.answer: Yes. Inspect the version control diff, verify expected changes, and rerun relevant checks before accepting the report.
